verdicts.evidence: paper/PAPER.md:146–162 separates pairwise support from numerical marginals, replaces the false converse with Proposition 6, and supplies primal/dual LP bounds. The six-profile counterexample now correctly excludes 000 and 111 despite its full pairwise hull. The independent rerun reproduced the exhaustive comparisons and certificate checks.

paper/PAPER.md:9,19,78–80 restricts the product-space result to domains where every answer combination is admissible. Line 206 explicitly distinguishes empirical correlation and respondent-distance maps from commitment compatibility graphs and explains their information loss.

simulation/fetch_data.py:136–156 retains screening fields; simulation/atlas/empirical.py:190–215 applies researcher and repeat-participation screening. The rerun reproduces 307 submissions, 232 eligible submissions, 166 eligible conference attendees, and 223 complete respondents in each battery, matching paper/PAPER.md:174.

simulation/atlas/empirical.py:32–49 replaces the independent-fold variance with (1/J + n_test/n_train) times the fold-score variance and uses t intervals. The corrected estimates at paper/PAPER.md:180,188,190 reproduce, including standard errors 0.061 and 0.178. This is an approximate resampling correction, appropriately attributed to Nadeau and Bengio.

paper/PAPER.md:176,194 distinguishes prespecified-triplet power from discovery power. simulation/atlas/empirical.py:384–473 reruns penalty selection, fitting, Monte Carlo testing and multiplicity correction on simulated datasets. With 9,999 draws, the minimum p-value is 0.0001, below 0.05/165. The rerun reproduces zero planted-effect discoveries in 100 trolley-size simulations and the approximately 0.059-bit discovery threshold.

paper/PAPER.md:9,21,192–194,210 replaces exclusion and impossibility claims with non-detection and limited sensitivity. It reports approximate simultaneous Wald intervals and simulated detection probabilities without treating prospective power as evidence that stronger effects are absent.

paper/PAPER.md:45–49 now requires an actual closure system containing the domain and closed under arbitrary intersections. The fallback closure is removed, the obstruction-free convention is explicit, and the open-interval counterexample is explained.
paper/PAPER.md:9,19 assigns order n+1 to categorical answers together with implications. Line 86 retains the correct order-one statement for implications alone.

new_problems.problem: The new assertion that the harmonic-corrected screening is valid under any dependence overlooks calibration of the individual p-values. The correction requires valid null p-values; simulating from a penalized model fitted to the same observations does not establish that requirement. Retain a nominal description or establish calibration before claiming guaranteed FDR control.
new_problems.evidence: Rechecked Benjamini–Yekutieli Theorem 1.3 and its proof, including the null-p-value condition on pp. 1180–1182. An independent check used the manuscript's pairwise-battery null: H is Bernoulli(0.1), with three conditionally independent answers having endorsement probability 0.9 when H=1 and 0.1 otherwise. This four-variable distribution has only pairwise log-linear terms. Using 223 observations, the supplied penalty-selection and Monte Carlo routines, 9,999 draws, and the harmonic correction, 75 of 1,000 datasets produced a discovery: estimated error probability 0.075, Wilson 95% interval 0.0603–0.0930. Under the manuscript's stated global pairwise-null interpretation, these are false discoveries. Reproduction script: /tmp/bpd-review-round4/calibration_mc.py; seeds 750000–750999. [Source theorem](https://www.math.tau.ac.il/~ybenja/MyPapers/benjamini_yekutieli_ANNSTAT2001.pdf).

contribution_after.assessment: The paper connects established Helly, constraint-satisfaction, marginal-polytope and information-decomposition results, with reproducible descriptive reanalyses and exhaustive small-case comparisons. The LP extension correctly applies existing facial-set theory and repairs the central false claim; its computational comparisons add useful evidence, while the screening's claimed error-control guarantee still needs correction.

summary: All eight original findings are closed. The full rerun passes 34 tests and reproduces the substantive results, and all 25 pages are visually clean. A new major FDR-calibration overclaim and two minor reporting/coverage problems remain. The abstract has 246 words; the availability section is present and its repository resolves; no prohibited self-reference was found. All six added references were checked against Crossref. Of 69 source verdicts, 68 are preserved unchanged and one was rechecked as noted.
